Great product if you are looking to make your own espresso at home without having to buy costly pods. I am a total espresso addict and having to drive to starbucks on my day off just to bring a coffee home to have with breakfast is a real pain in the butt not to mention costly. The pods you can buy for the nespresso machine are also costly and produce a lot of waste, if you care about the environment this is not the best option. I recently bought these refillable nespresso pods for just that reason. They work great, allow me to use my favorite espresso that is not available in pods and the cost is much less for buying espresso in bulk and also produces a lot less waste. The pod did take me a few tries to get right, but I emailed the seller and got feedback very quickly. Here is a  helpful tip that I have learned: Do not overfill the pods, the first few I tried them I packed the espresso in tight and ended up only getting a spurt of coffee then water. Fill the pod lightly, do not pack down and leave a tiny amount of space between the espresso and the lid. If you shake the store bought espresso pods you will hear movement inside the pod, your refillable pods should have the same sound. Once you get your filling technique down, it's super quick and simple. This product saves money and produces a lot less waste, I highly recommend everyone with a nespresso get these refillable pods.

When looking for a lower cost alternative to the LG OEM water filter I came across the Waterdrop WD-LT700P replacement water filter. The filter was shipped quickly and arrived undamaged, the filter itself was sealed to prevent contamination. I installed the filter just as I would the OEM filter without any issues. I ran about 2.5 gallons of water thru the dispenser to clear the system and charge the filter. I then tasted the water and it tasted pretty good. Other than taste I looked at the Ice cubes the next day and they appeared a little clearer to me. . I have no way of testing the water for chemicals and such.

According the insert that came with the Waterdrop filter it states that "this filter is Tested and Certified by NSF international against NSF/ANSI Standard 42".
The LG OEM filter that I normally buy states its filter is "Tested and Certified by NSF international against NSF/ANSI Standard 42 and Standard 53". It also come with a California Department of Public Health certificate.

For references:
NSF/ANSI Standard 42 (aesthetics) applies to these contaminants: Chlorine, Chloramine, Bad Tastes, Odors, Sediment.
NSF/ANSI Standard 53 (health effects) for the reduction of specific health-related contaminants, such as cysts (Cryptosporidium, Giardia, Entamoeba, and Toxoplasma), lead, and volatile organic chemicals (Pesticides, Herbicides, or Insecticides)
